raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not want to toss money around or try fancy things. I still look first at what worked on my own land and what the nearby families are doing. On my 6.5 mu, I will keep most land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steady way here, and keep a small piece in cotton for cash. I cannot manage too much labor with only two people in the house, so I will do things the familiar way, use the well when the crop really needs it, and not push fertilizer too hard because pumping and fertilizer both cost money. For wheat already in the field, I will topdress once more if the stand looks a little pale, then give water around jointing and maybe once near filling if spring stays dry. After wheat harvest I will plant maize right away on the same land, no delay, because the window is short. Cotton I will keep on the smaller piece, with moderate fertilizer and a couple of irrigations, because cotton needs watching and hand work, and at my age I cannot expand it too much.
